name: War Inc: Rising Beginner Guide — How to Start Strong in 2026
title: War Inc: Rising Beginner Guide — Tips, Strategy and Progression | War Inc: Rising Wiki
meta_description: New to War Inc: Rising? This complete beginner guide covers daily routine, building priority, gem spending, 16 mistakes to avoid, and a week-by-week progression path to level up fast.
author: War Inc Wiki Team
excerpt: Everything you need to know as a new player — from daily routine and building priority to gem spending, common mistakes, and a full progression roadmap covering your first week through month 3+.

sections.heading: Your Daily Routine in War Inc: Rising
sections.content:
Building good daily habits is the fastest way to progress. The game resets every day at 5PM Mountain / 7PM Eastern / Midnight GMT. Here is exactly what to do each day.

Step 1: Collect your buildings. Open the building icon (bottom left) and collect from your Gold Mine (gold), Sawmill (wood), extra wood building, and Castle (gems). Start your next upgrade immediately — always prioritize the Castle.

Step 2: Complete daily quests. You get 5 quests per day with 24 hours to complete them. You also get 3 resets per day if a quest requires troops you don't have. Don't forget weekly and seasonal quests (2-4 week duration) for bigger rewards.

Step 3: Use your free battles. You get 3 free Hunting battles and 3 free Infinite War battles per day. Using gems for extra battles is almost never worth it unless you are competing for top leaderboard positions.

Step 4: Collect free stuff. Claim free items from the shop, check the events tab for limited-time rewards, and sign in daily for event rewards like scrolls, chests, and even Frost Queen shards.

sections.heading: Building Priority — What to Upgrade First
sections.content:
Your buildings determine your passive income and troop power. Upgrade them in this exact order for maximum efficiency.

1. Castle (Command Center) — Your absolute top priority. Spend ALL your wood on upgrading the castle. Each level gives +50 troop energy, which is massive. One castle level is worth roughly 10 dragons' worth of power.

2. Spell Cauldron — Unlocks at certain castle levels. Provides spell capacity for battle.

3. Gold Mine — Passive gold income. Gold is essential for recruitment and dice rolling in co-op. Keep it at a reasonable level.

4. Sawmill — Produces wood for castle upgrades. Only upgrade enough to keep castle construction going.

5. Follower Camp — Lowest priority. Leave it at level 1 until you have everything else maxed.

Daily building routine: Collect everything, start your next castle upgrade, then queue other buildings. Castle first, always.

sections.heading: Gem Spending Guide — What to Spend Your Gems On
sections.content:
Gems are the most valuable currency in War Inc: Rising. Spending them wisely makes or breaks your account progression.

The Wheel is your best gem value. Stop at milestone chests (10, 30, 50, 100 pulls) to keep your cost per mythic low. Card Master is also good — roughly 250 gems per pull with a 1 in 12 chance for the featured mythic. On average it takes 6.5 picks to get the specific mythic you want.

If you spend real money, the 30-Day Premium Pass ($15/month) is the best value at 2,000 gems upfront plus 320 gems per day. The Battle Pass ($10 every 2 weeks) is also solid. Growth Packs ($1 to $2) each give a mythic troop and are excellent value for light spenders.

Save your gems for good mythic rotations on the Wheel and Card Master. Do not spend gems on extra battles, fusion, or regular recruitment.

sections.heading: Gem Spending — What NOT to Waste Gems On
sections.content:
Avoiding bad gem purchases is just as important as making good ones. Here is what to never spend gems on.

Extra Infinite War and Hunting battles are a trap. The 3 free daily battles are enough. Extra battles cost gems and give minimal returns unless you are a top-tier player.

Fusion with gems is outdated advice. The old guide recommended gem fusion but the updated community consensus is clear: only use gold for fusion. Never spend gems on it.

Do not use gems for regular recruitment or summoning. Use gold and scrolls for this instead.

Avoid non-mythic wheels entirely. Only spin wheels that feature the mythic troops you need.

Speed-ups and building resources bought with gems are terrible value. Time is free — let buildings complete naturally.

sections.heading: Early Game Priorities — Your First Month
sections.content:
Your first 30 days set the foundation for everything. Focus on these five things.

1. Castle upgrades. Every piece of wood goes into the castle. Each level is a massive power spike for your whole army.

2. Get Oracles. They are pound-for-pound the best epic in the game. Each Oracle gives a 4% attack buff to nearby allies, and the buff stacks up to 20 layers. Get as many Oracles as you can.

3. Build 8-10 level 6 Poison Masters. They will carry you through mid-game Infinite War and most PvE content.

4. Fuse Bombs using gold. Fuse 3 level 6 uncommon troops together for a chance at a Bomb. Bombs are dominant in the 2,500-5,000 trophy range.

5. Get Goddess of War. She is essential support that fits into every formation. Her shield protects your key damage dealers.

sections.heading: Mid Game Priorities — Month 1 to 3
sections.content:
Once you have your early game foundation, shift focus to building a roster of S-tier mythics.

Radiant Warrior is your top priority. Get two copies and keep them at the same level. Never merge your last two copies. His shield and massive HP make him the best tank in the game.

Frost Queen is equally important. Same rule applies — keep two copies at the same level. Her AoE damage dominates PvP.

Bone Marksman should reach level 4 as a minimum. His skill unlocks at level 4, making him a pseudo-level 6 at only level 4. His stat scaling doubles from 1 to 2 to 3 to 4, then drops off.

Light Seeker is your PvP destroyer. His Holy Wash ability heals him and damages enemies when his HP drops below 50%. At level 4, Light Volley gives multi-shot with a +50% attack buff.

Necromancer is your PvE king. He summons skeleton swarms that absorb damage and deals massive damage to bosses. Pair him with Goddess of War to keep his skeletons alive.

sections.heading: Late Game Goals — Month 3 and Beyond
sections.content:
After three months, you should be competing at a high level. Here is what to work toward.

Take Ursa and Elven Archer to level 7 with forge stones. They are the best legendary investments for forge stone upgrades.

Upgrade your epics to level 8+. Focus on Oracles, Flame Mages, and Poison Masters. These troops are used everywhere and benefit hugely from extra levels.

Push specific rares to level 9. Forest Scouts, Shove Boy, and Bombs are the best rare troops worth taking all the way to level 9.

Get into the Ruler system for clan wars. Ruler equipment from core stones adds significant power to your clan war formations.

Build multiple S+ tier mythics at level 4 or higher. Having 3-4 top-tier mythics gives you flexibility across all game modes.

sections.heading: 16 Common Mistakes New Players Make
sections.content:
Avoid these mistakes to save weeks of wasted progress.

1. Using forge stones on the wrong troops. Save forge stones for Ursa, Elven Archer, Oracles, and Flame Mages. Never waste them on commons or rares you will not use long-term.

2. Not picking a Dragon Clash side immediately. The event runs periodically. Join a side the moment it starts. Missing even one day of quests wastes valuable rewards.

3. Merging your last two copies of strong troops. Never merge your last two Radiant Warriors, Frost Queens, or any S-tier troop. Two level 3s are better than one level 4. Keep at least two copies at the same level.

4. Spending gems on the wrong things. Extra battles, fusion, and speed-ups are all gem traps. Only spend on the Wheel and Card Master.

5. Forgetting the name color trick. You can make your name any color using the format <#RGB> with 3-digit hex codes. Check borderleft.com/toolbox/hex for colors.

6. Ignoring the Trial feature in clan war. You can hit towers, gates, dragons, and spiders for FREE to test formations. No morale cost. Always trial before committing real attacks.

7. Not coordinating dragon times in clan war. Dragon diplomacy with neighboring teams is essential. Agree on 30-minute time slots so everyone gets a fair chance at dragon damage.

8. Not using the Rope-a-Dope technique in Crimson Moon. Move your formation out of your tower, let the enemy hit (they lose extra morale), then move back in and attack them as the attacker.

9. Spending all your gold at once. Stay near the gold cap but do not waste natural regeneration. Use gold on recruitment when you are near the cap.

10. Using uncommons in your main formation. Uncommons are fusion material, not usable troops. Fuse them away for a chance at Bombs.

11. Only recruiting at level 3. Level 1 recruitment gives mastery points toward mastery chests. Balance between level 1 and level 3 recruiting.

12. Not checking the Discord for event schedules. The official Discord has +wheel, +summon, and +cardmaster commands showing upcoming schedules. Use it to plan your gem spending.

13. Not understanding multi-unit vs single-unit stats. The health and attack shown is per individual troop in a squad, not the total. A Berserker with 8 individuals shows per-troop stats. A single-unit like Goblin Chef shows actual stats. This completely changes how you evaluate troops.

14. Wasting forge stones on level 7 commons. Level 7 commons unlock Trigger Master, but forge stones are too precious. Only upgrade one common to level 7 for the 100-gem Power Stance achievement.

15. Using Wood Shield Guard. This common is trash tier — a single-unit common with terrible stats. Use Swordsman instead (multi-unit with splash damage).

16. Using Snowball Thrower or Gunner. Archer is the only common range worth using. The elemental damage on other common ranges is too low to matter.

sections.heading: Progression Path — Week by Week
sections.content:
Week 1-2: Focus entirely on castle upgrades. Complete all daily quests. Save your gems — do not spend them yet. Start collecting Oracles and Poison Masters as your core team.

Week 3-4: Start using gems on the Wheel when good mythic rotations appear. Build up Bombs through uncommon fusion with gold. Join an active clan — look for clans on the official Discord. Begin co-op grinding with a partner.

Month 2: Target specific mythics like Radiant Warrior and Frost Queen. Push to 2,500-5,000 trophies where Bombs dominate. Participate in clan war to learn the basics. Join Dragon Clash events when they run.

Month 3+: Level 7 your best epics and legendaries with forge stones. Enter the Ruler system for clan war. Build multiple S-tier mythics to level 4+. Aim for top 1,000 in arena. Get active in clan leadership and diplomacy.

sections.heading: Understanding Troop Stats — Multi-Unit vs Single-Unit
sections.content:
This is the most misunderstood mechanic in War Inc: Rising and it completely changes how you evaluate troops.

Multi-unit troops (like Berserker with 8 individuals, or Forest Scouts) display their stats PER INDIVIDUAL, not as a total. A Berserker showing 1,000 HP actually has 8,000 total HP across all 8 units. Multi-unit troops are better for triggering abilities and dealing spread damage.

Single-unit troops (like Goblin Chef, Wood Shield Guard, or Radiant Warrior) show their ACTUAL stats. What you see is what you get. Single-unit troops are better as tanks, heavy hitters, and units where you need concentrated power.

This distinction matters most when comparing troops of different types. A multi-unit troop with lower per-unit stats might actually have higher total HP and damage. Always consider the unit count when evaluating a troop's true power.

sections.heading: Useful Resources for New Players
sections.content:
Bookmark these resources to accelerate your progression.

Official Discord — Use commands like +wheel, +summon, and +cardmaster to check upcoming schedules. This is the best way to plan your gem spending.

Top Clan Discords — Clans like Mortal Crowns and Heretic Sanctuary have public channels with strategy guides, template formations, tier lists, and experienced players who answer questions.

Name Color Tool — borderleft.com/toolbox/hex provides 3-digit hex codes for customizing your in-game name color. Format is <#RGB>.

Community Tier Lists — Check this wiki's hero tier lists for the latest community rankings from Klown Kollege and other top players.

mainEntity.name: What should I spend gems on in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spend gems on the Wheel (best value, stop at milestone chests) and Card Master. Never spend gems on extra battles, fusion, speed-ups, or regular recruitment.

mainEntity.name: What is the best building to upgrade first in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Castle (Command Center) is always the top priority. Each level gives +50 troop energy. Spend all your wood on castle upgrades.

mainEntity.name: What are the best early game troops in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Focus on getting Oracles (best epic), 8-10 level 6 Poison Masters, Bombs via fusion, and Goddess of War. These will carry you through your first month.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth spending gems on fusion in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only use gold for fusion. Using gems on fusion is outdated advice from an older game version.

mainEntity.name: How do I get more forge stones in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Forge stones come from Infinite War rewards, Hunting rewards, daily chests, summon events, and the shop. Save them for impactful upgrades on Ursa, Elven Archer, Oracles, and Flame Mages.
